newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: JP Morgan buys share in Venezuelan Banco Mercantil.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan buys share in Venezuelan Banco Mercantil.

text.p: J.P. Morgan Capital, a fully-owned subsidiary of J.P. Morgan & Co Inc bought a 9.65 percent share of leading Venezuelan bank Banco Mercantil on Monday, Banco Mercantil said.
Morgan Capital bought 10.61 million Class B shares on the Caracas stock exchange, at a price of 1,347 bolivars ($2.82) per share. Class B shares have lesser voting rights than Class A shares.
"We're exceptionally pleased with Morgan Capital's investment," said Mercantil President Gustavo Maturet in a press statement.

"Other than strengthening Mercantil ... it increases foreign investor participation (in the bank) ... and recognizes the strategy we have been pursuing in Venezuela's increasingly competitive banking market," Maturet added.

Morgan Capital's investment in Banco Mercantil, Venezuela's second largest bank, came after Spanish banks Banco Santander and Bilbao Vizcaya each bought controlling stakes in Mercantil's leading local competitors earlier this year.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya bought a 40 percent share in Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial in early March, while Banco Santander bought a 93 percent stake in Banco de Venezuela, Venezuela's third largest bank, in January.
